subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex app-server WebSocket and Unix connection establishment use an unconditional 30-second deadline, or should that deadline derive from an existing owner-approved timeout budget?
rationale: Current behavior has no connection-establishment deadline, while the documented 60-second `requestTimeoutMs` applies to control-plane calls after connection; choosing a fixed 30-second cutoff therefore changes compatibility and operator expectations rather than merely correcting an implementation detail.

options.title: Approve the fixed 30 seconds
options.body: Keep the bounded shared constant because it avoids new config, matches established handshake floors, and gives stalled connections a deterministic failure path.

options.title: Reuse the request budget
options.body: Pass the resolved app-server request timeout into transport creation so operators retain one timeout budget, while explicitly documenting that it now also bounds connection establishment.

options.title: Add a connection-specific setting
options.body: Introduce a dedicated plugin-owned connection timeout only if remote deployments demonstrably require independent tuning and the added config surface is accepted.

recommendation.title: Approve the fixed 30 seconds
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded shared constant because it avoids new config, matches established handshake floors, and gives stalled connections a deterministic failure path.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and merged the Codex extension transport/client boundary and is the strongest available owner for its connection-lifecycle policy.
